Given that the triangle $△ABC$ above is an equilateral triangle and $AH=40,$ what is the length of $\overset{―}{AC}?$
question.worked_solution:
Let's draw triangle $△ABH,$ which is a ${30}^{∘}$-${60}^{∘}$-${90}^{∘}$ triangle.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14165760/assets/7cbfe29dd9087d07b6d2101e85b9154836704221320f4dd19346f49f3a858fa3.png)

 

Since the longer leg, $\overset{―}{AH},$ has a length of $40,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3}x & =40 \\ x & =\frac{40}{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{40}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{40\sqrt{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We can now calculate the length of the hypotenuse, $\overset{―}{AB},$ as follows:

$$
AB=2x=2\cdot \frac{40\sqrt{3}}{3}=\frac{80\sqrt{3}}{3}.
$$

Finally, since $△ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, we get

$$
AC=AB=\frac{80\sqrt{3}}{3}.
$$
